brief: UBS's Simon Penn argues politics, not macro, is now the primary market driver after the Democratic midterm sweep raised the odds of curbs on AI/datacenter investment, which supplies about half of 2.2% y/y Q2 GDP growth. UBS sees the real risk as a financing bubble, not an end-demand bust: 2027 datacenter capacity is already permitted and under construction, but the top-13 hyperscalers face a roughly $300bn 2027 funding gap against $1.77trn capex, and any capex slowdown would relieve memory-chip supply shortages, which Asian memory stocks already appear to be pricing. Separately, Thursday's selloff re-correlated US equities (SPX -4.7%, VIX +12pts to 29), hitting semis hardest; UBS still targets SPX 8100 year-end and recommends a call-spread. UBS forecasts October CPI below consensus, so December FOMC hike odds swung from 80% to 60% on the selloff then back to 20bp after a hot payrolls print, which also drove a USD safe-haven bid, hurting G10 FX more than EM. China tech is rebounding as a hedge-fund short-China/long-memory pair trade unwinds. The BoE hiked to 4.00% reluctantly, blaming energy and the Iran war for inflation rather than demand.
